competency_fulfillment.rationale: Each item sets a half against a quarter and asks which relation holds, and the keys are correct in both directions, so the comparison the competency names is what is being scored.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both orderings are generated - the half presented first and the quarter presented first - so pupils cannot succeed by always choosing the same symbol, which is the main trap for a two-fraction comparison.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The stems carry raw LaTeX fraction markup rather than the plain slash notation used in the neighbouring fraction nodes of this same quarter; if that markup reaches a Grade 1 screen unrendered, a six-year-old is looking at backslashes and braces instead of a fraction.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All nine samples are one task with three interchangeable wordings; nothing asks which shaded model is larger, or has the pupil point to the greater part, so the models the competency requires are only referred to, never acted on.

competency_alignment.rationale: Since only one fraction pair exists in this competency, what differs between seeds is stem phrasing and option order rather than any growth in comparison demand, and the correct answer is always one of exactly two symbols.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The quantities compared are precisely the half and the quarter the competency specifies, with no additional denominators pulled in from later grades.
